title: The power that divides thought into letters: why speech, the higher, comes last
overview:
Chapter 41 described the levels of thought; chapter 42 asks where the power comes from that divides an idea into combinations of letters. In *bina* an idea is one thing, even in its depth: a car designer thinks "a car". To improve it he must cut it into seats, wheels and screws, and then write it down. That cutting is the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*, carved like letters out of a rubber stamp. It looks like a descent, but its root is above the grasp: a baby knows which dish he likes as well as the chef, and cannot say why until he can talk. So "a *katan* has no thought" means no letters of thought.

The combining of the pieces comes from *chachma*, by itself, as long as the speaker keeps the thread of the whole. And speech, rooted in *chachma*, is higher than thought and therefore comes last; that is why teaching and saying the words wake up the thought, and why the symbol comes before the thing: the *Aibershter* wanted *matza*, so He made *Pesach*.

sections.title: Where the power to divide thought into letters comes from: the five gevuros of Ima
sections.summary: The chapter asks where the power comes from that divides an idea into combinations of letters in thought. The answer is the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*: the *tzimtzum* in *bina* that cuts the one idea into pieces, as letters are carved out of a rubber stamp.

phrases.he: (מב) ומעתה יובן בענין שרש כח המחלק לצירופי אותיות דמחשבה במדריגה הג', כשחושב ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים, מאין הוא בא כח ההתחלקות זאת
אך הנה ידוע דבחינת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דאימא הוא שרש כח ההתחלקות הזאת כו'.
וביאור הדברים ידוע, דבחינת אימא הוא בחינת בינה והשגה לאורך ורוחב בהסבר דבר המושכל
וכאשר הוא מעיין בבחינת העומק של ההשגה, עדיין הוא רק בעומק מחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל, שלמעלה מהיות בחינת התחלקות צירופי אותיות ממש במחשבה להשכלת הענין,
רק בחינת מחשבה שכל בלבד כנראה בחוש
phrases.en: It's actually the inner *machshava* of the mind; it's not yet actually an external *machshava* of separate letters.

blocks.text: The chapter asks where the power comes from that divides the letters of thought into combinations, at the third level, when a person thinks a matter through in different combinations. The known answer is the five *gevuros* (powers of restraint) of *Ima* (the mother). *Ima* is *bina* (understanding), the grasp of an idea in length and breadth. Even when one looks into the depth of that grasp, it is still only *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought): the inner *machshava* (thought) of the mind, **not yet actually an external *machshava* of separate letters**.

phrases.he: אך על ידי בחינת ה׳ גבורות, שהוא בחינת הצמצום והסתלקות שבכח ההשגה עצמה, להיות יורד אור השכלת הענין שבמחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל לבחינת התחלקות צירופים שונים בפרטי פרטיות כו'
phrases.en: This brings out, through the power of *tzimtzum* of *bina*, the ability to cut it up into particular *inyanim* that can be analyzed.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא בחינת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דאימא, שנקרא פתוחי חותם כו'
phrases.en: This is what's called the five *gevuros* of *Ima*, *pituchei chosam*: the *pituchim* of the seal, carve out the seal.

blocks.text: The five *gevuros* are the *tzimtzum* (contraction) and withdrawal within the power of grasp itself, and through them the light of the idea comes down into many different combinations. When a person thinks about an idea, his inner thought is about the idea as a whole; the *tzimtzum* of *bina* brings out **the ability to cut it up into particular *inyanim* that can be analyzed**. This is called the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* (the five final letters) of *Ima*.

blocks.title: The rubber stamp
blocks.text: It is also called *pituchei chosam*, the carvings of a seal. Think of the stamp the bank gives you to put on the back of your check. It starts as a plain piece of rubber, and they carve the letters out of it.

The idea starts in the mind as one main thing. Even in the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept) it is still singular, not yet cut up into separate things. This is not *chachma* (wisdom), where it is singular as an *ayin* (nothing); it is the idea once it is a *yesh* (something), an actual understanding of a certain thing.

blocks.title: Addition
blocks.text: When you think of addition, you think of it as one single thing. Only when you go to explain it to somebody, and that includes thinking up new ways of adding or deeper matters in it, which you first have to explain to yourself, must you be *metzamtzem* (contract): keep certain parts and cut others away. That is *pituchei chosam*: a stamp is made by keeping some parts and cutting away the rest, and that is how the letters come out.

Whether to explain it to someone else or to oneself, a *machshava iyunis* has to be dressed in the external thought of letters. The real *machshevas sechel* (thought of the intellect), before it comes into that external thought, is one singular thing.

blocks.title: The car designer
blocks.text: Take a car. A car designer thinks of a car as a car, just as someone who knows nothing about cars does, but he knows a great deal more about it. When he thinks of it, it is, as a listener put it, one holistic idea not analyzed yet: the *tamtzis* (essence) of the whole thing, the *omek hamusag*. Now he wants to come up with improvements, next year's model, and make a few million dollars on it. When he first sits down to it, the whole car is in his mind as a *tamtzis*.

blocks.title: The car designer
blocks.text: It is a *tamtzis*, not a *kitzur*: the *kitzur* (shortening) is the short idea before the *iyun* (analysis), the *tamtzis* the idea after it. Even so, to design a better car he must cut it into teeny pieces. He cannot improve the whole car at once: think real hard, meditate, do the breathing exercises, and poof, here is the 2005 model. It doesn't work like that. He takes it apart into its components: the seats, the wheels, the screws on the wheels, what the wheels are made of, the grooves in them; maybe we should change the grooves.

That is the *MNTzPCh* of *bina*. The *gevuros* means he makes *tzimtzumim* in the idea: to think about the seat, he cuts away the whole car and leaves only the seat, as with the seal, where you cut away everything around it and leave the letter.

sections.title: Cutting the idea into letters looks like a descent, but its root is above the grasp
sections.summary: Bringing the whole idea down to pieces, and then to letters, looks like a descent, yet the power to do it is rooted higher than the grasp of the idea itself. The proof is a small child, who can tell one thing from another before he has letters in his thought.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שלכאורה בחינת ירידה וצמצום הוא,
phrases.en: At first glance it looks like really a *yerida* and a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אבל שרשו בא מלמעלה מכח ההשגה שבגוף המושכל הזה כו'
phrases.en: The fact that he can do that is higher than even the actual *sechel* of the car itself.

blocks.text: **At first glance it looks like really a *yerida* and a *tzimtzum***, a descent: he had the whole essential image of the car in his mind, its *tamtzis*, and now he has brought it down to some little thing like the seat. But its root comes from above the power of grasp in the idea itself.

He turns the idea into little pieces and symbolizes them all the way down to letters: to improve the car, thinking is not enough; he must write a report, notes to himself or to other car geniuses. **The fact that he can do that is higher than even the actual *sechel* of the car itself.**

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שאנו רואים בתינוק קטן שאין בו עדיין צירופי אותיות במחשבתו בדבר פרטי כמו גם דבר מה שנותנין לו,
הגם שמבחין בו
phrases.en: He does have the *havchana*.

phrases.he: ולא יחליפנו בדבר אחר כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: He likes *davka* this one.

phrases.he: שזה הוא התחלקות המחשבה,
phrases.en: He does have the *hischalkus hamachshava* of *bina*.

phrases.he: אבל לא בצירופי אותיות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: But not all the way to bring it out into an external *machshava*.

phrases.he: הנה מכל מקום
phrases.en: Nonetheless,

phrases.he: כאשר יכול לדבר ולבקש בפה לדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: Once he already can talk and ask with his mouth for a particular thing,

phrases.he: הרי אז יש לו בודאי במוח מחשבתו צירופי אותיות פרטיים לאותו דבר פרטי שמבקש בדבור

blocks.title: The toy car
blocks.text: The proof is a small child, who has no combinations of letters in his thought yet. Give a little kid a toy car: he likes this one and not the other, so he can tell the difference. But he cannot bring out in words why, though there is a reason. The people who design toys want to find those reasons: know why the boys like this car and the girls this doll, and you can make a lot of money.

So the child has the essential *sechel* (intellect): it is what the toy designers are looking into, even though he cannot break it up into explanations. You see he has it, because he likes this car and not that one. That is the *havchana* (discernment) of *bina*, as in "Who gave the rooster *bina* to distinguish between day and night."

What he lacks is letters in his thought for the particular thing. He has the *havchana*, he likes *davka* (precisely) this one and will not take another for it, and he has the *hischalkus* (division) of thought, **but not all the way to bring it out into an external *machshava***. Nonetheless, **once he already can talk and ask with his mouth for a particular thing**, he surely has in his mind the combinations of letters for the thing he asks for.

sections.title: The letters are divided in thought before speech, and speech is what divides them
sections.summary: To speak, a child must first have the letters divided in his thought; yet it is speech that brings about the division of thought: the voice of the turtledove is heard in speech, and the mother lends her clothing to her daughter. The class opens on direct and symbolic thought.

phrases.he: כי צירופי אותיות מתחלקות במחשבה תחלה טרם בואם לדבור
phrases.en: The *tzirufei osios* has to be separated out in the mind first before you can talk.

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר דעקבי לאה נכנסין תוך ראש רחל, דהיינו דבור שבמחשבה הנזכר לעיל שנעשה מחשבה לדבור כו')
וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין מאמר הזהר על פסוק וקול התור נשמע בארצינו,
דוקא בבחינת הדבור
phrases.en: It's heard *davka* in *dibur*: the voice of the inner *machshava* of the thing is heard *davka* in the *dibur*.

phrases.he: אז זמן התחלקות אותיות המחשבה כו'
phrases.en: It's *davka* the *dibur* that brings about the *hischalkus* of the *machshava*.

phrases.he: (והיינו ענין כללות המאמר דאימא אוזיפת דרך שאלה ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך לברתא,
phrases.en: This is the general *inyan* of what it says, that the mother loans her clothes in a way of a loan, the five *gevuros*, to her daughter,

phrases.he: שהוא צירופי התחלקות אותיות הדבור כו')
phrases.en: which is the putting together of the separations of the letters of speech.

blocks.title: Just a symbol
blocks.text: What the chapter is about is direct thought against symbolic thought. People say, "Oh, that's just semantics." In matters of *frumkeit*, the Reform and people like that try to reduce these things to a symbol: *Pesach* and the *matzos* are just a symbol, so why make such a big deal of it? Of course, sit down and eat *matza*, and then drink a beer; the main thing is that you did the symbolism. The general idea is that the rituals of religion are just symbols. It is also the universalism of the Greeks, the matter of *Chanuka*: all religions are really the same, except you use these symbols and I use these.
blocks.outOfPlace: Opens class 215, before line 11 is read: it introduces what the chapter is about.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks the Reform view of ritual (eat matza, then drink a beer).

The main thing, they say, is that you did the symbolism. The general idea is that the rituals of religion are just symbols. It is also the universalism of the Greeks, the matter of *Chanuka*: all religions are really the same, except you use these symbols and I use these.

blocks.text: This is what the text is talking about: turning the thing into letters, so that a group of letters in a certain order stands for an actual concept. A little kid has the concept before he has the symbolic ability to represent it in letters, and this proves that the symbolic ability comes from a higher place than the *etzem* (essence) of thinking the concept.
blocks.outOfPlace: The opening of class 215, just before it reads line 11.

blocks.text: A child who talks has the *tzirufei osios* (combinations of letters) in his mind, for **the *tzirufei osios* has to be separated out in the mind first before you can talk**: the heels of Leah enter the head of Rachel. And as the *Zohar* says on "the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land", the voice of the inner *machshava* **is heard *davka* in the *dibur***: speech brings about the *hischalkus* of thought.

This is the general meaning of the saying that **the mother loans her clothes in a way of a loan**, the five *gevuros*, **to her daughter**: the putting together of the separations of the letters of speech.

sections.title: The combinations are rooted above the grasp, and Abba puts them together by itself
sections.summary: A baby tastes as well as a chef but cannot say why: dividing an idea into letters is rooted above the grasp of *bina*, in the source of its depth. Putting the pieces together comes from *chachma*, the power that combines automatically, which is why a speaker who loses the whole loses his thread.

phrases.he: ואם כן מזה ראיה שאין הצירופים שרשם בהשגה עצמה
phrases.en: From this, we see that the *tzirufim*, turning the concept into the symbolic words, are not really rooted in the actual understanding itself.

phrases.he: שהרי התינוק מבחין ומשיג בין טוב לרע גם טרם שיכול לדבר,
phrases.en: He already can tell you the difference between things, what he likes and what he doesn't like.

phrases.he: ואף על פי כן אין לו צירופי אותיות במחשבתו עד שיכול לדבר דוקא כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: So the *tzirufim* (combinations), turning the concept into symbolic words, **are not really rooted in the actual understanding itself**. For a child tells good from bad before he can talk: **he already can tell you the difference between things, what he likes and what he doesn't like**.

blocks.title: The baby and the chef
blocks.text: A baby tastes a food and knows right away that it is fantastic, and that another food he doesn't like. As far as the *hasaga* (grasp) goes, he knows exactly what the chef knows, every nuance of the taste. What he cannot do is separate it into pieces and say which part he likes. The chef can, because he reaches up into something higher than the *hasaga*: he separates it out until he can sit down and write you a recipe, a little cumin, a tiny drop of lemon. The child tastes the cumin and the lemon and likes them; he just doesn't know what they are.

blocks.title: The baby and the chef
blocks.text: Give him the same dish from another chef who did not follow the same recipe, and he says, "Eh, that's not so good." He knows as well as any grown-up which one tasted lousy and which one great. So the division comes from higher: bringing it all down to little pieces, and further still, symbolizing them until you can write them down in words. The word "cumin" is not the actual cumin; it only stands for it. The actual cumin even the kid can taste.
And still, the line goes on, he has no combinations of letters in his thought until he can speak, *davka*. The class stops over the printed text here, which has a gap before *davka*.

phrases.he: אלא שרשם מלמעלה מן ההשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: The *shoresh* of the actual separation into letters is higher than the actual *hasaga*, the actual understanding of what the concept is all about.

phrases.he: והוא מבחינת כח ומקור של כל עומק ההשגה כו'
phrases.en: It is really from the *koach* and *makor* of that whole depth of the *hasaga*.

phrases.he: (כמו שבאותיות הדבור שרש כח הצירופים מאבא, דהיינו מפנימיות החכמה, שהוא כח המשכיל דחכמה שנקרא קדמות השכל (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין תרין ציפרין כמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם)

blocks.text: The *shoresh* (root) of the separation into letters is above the *hasaga* of *bina*: **it is really from the *koach* and *makor* of that whole depth of the *hasaga***. As the combinations of speech are rooted in *Abba* (the father), the inside of *chachma*, so this is in the depths of the *koach hamaskil* (the power that brings insight), higher than *bina* itself.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך שבה' מוצאות הוא המחלק ומסדר הצירופים בדבור כפי אופן התחלקות צירופים שבמחשבה, ממש מה׳ גבורות דאימא הנזכר לעיל
מכל מקום אבא יסד
phrases.en: *Davka* the *chachma* is what puts together the speech.

phrases.he: בבחינת כח המצרף, שהוא בלתי כוונה בשכל והשגה איך לצרף, רק ממילא בא,
phrases.en: You don't have to put it together then. It comes together automatically.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב מצרף לחכמה וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר וכמו שיתבאר

blocks.text: The five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of the five places of articulation divide and order the combinations of speech after the division in thought, and they come from the *gevuros* of *Ima*. Even so, *Abba yasad*: **the *chachma* is what puts together the speech**, as the *koach hamatzref* (the power that combines), with no intention of the mind how to combine. When you think what to say, what you do is separate, with *bina*. **You don't have to put it together then. It comes together automatically.**

blocks.title: Taking apart a watch
blocks.text: Take apart a piece of machinery, a watch, and you have to figure out how to put it together again. Even there the *chachma* comes from the *bina*: if you take it apart properly, noting exactly how you did it, and not without looking at what you're doing, you will automatically know how to put it back together.

A teacher in class thinks what to say: how to separate out the matters. You would think he must also think how to put them back into a whole, coherent speech, or he will talk once about this and once about that and end up with little pieces of a car and no car. It doesn't work like that. All you think about is how to take it apart; it gets put together automatically, and the pieces follow one another into a coherent whole. That does not mean *chachma* does nothing; its work is automatic.

blocks.title: The thread of thought
blocks.text: As he will say later, it is like a necklace: beads or pearls with a string running through them, what is called in English the thread of thought. A person who loses the thread of his thought has lost sight of the overview of the whole idea. Then the whole thing falls apart and he doesn't know what to say next. He really has the next little piece in his mind, but he can't even say that, because he no longer remembers how the whole holds together.

In some places it says that memory comes from *chachma*. Rabbi Markel does not know exactly how, or in what part of the brain, but while *bina* cuts the idea into little pieces, *chachma* has to remember the whole: when you're talking about seats, you have to remember you're talking about a car.

Sometimes people talk, go off on a tangent, and then say, "Wait, wait, what were we talking about?" What do you mean, you don't know what you're talking about? He went off on a tangent. The tangent did fit into some whole, but he forgot the whole. And sometimes the tangent goes totally outside the whole, and then he literally cannot bring it back.

sections.title: Why a small child is said to have no thought
sections.summary: The combinations come through the *tzimtzum* of analytical thought, but the power that makes them is above that thought. So a child cannot think in words until he can speak, and "a *katan* has no thought" means no letters of thought, not no thinking.

phrases.he: ונמצא שגם שבחינת הצירופים עצמם שבמחשבה על ידי בחינת צמצום דמחשבה עיונית הוא בא, מכל מקום כח ושרש העושה לצירוף והתחלקות זאת,
הרי הוא למעלה מכח ההשגה שבמחשבה עיונית עצמה כו'
phrases.en: It's really higher than the *hisbonenus* itself.

phrases.he: שלזה הטעם אין התינוק יכול לצרף אותיות מחשבתו עד שיוכל לצרף אותיות הדבור,
phrases.en: Until he can talk he can't think in words either.

phrases.he: גם שמשיג ומבחין היטב בגוף הענין דבר מה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Even though he understands very well the actual whatever it is.

phrases.he: ואם כן הרי מה שאמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה,
היינו בבחינת צרופי אותיות המחשבה דוקא,
phrases.en: Meaning that he cannot think in words.

phrases.he: לפי ששרשם בא מכח ומקור של המחשבה דהשגה דבינה כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: The combinations come by the *tzimtzum* of *machshava iyunis*, but the power that makes them is **really higher than the *hisbonenus* itself**. So a child cannot think in words until he can talk, though he grasps the thing well. That a *katan* (a minor) has no thought does not mean he can't think: he knows this from that. He cannot think in words, whose root is the source of the thought of *bina*.

sections.title: Why thought comes before speech: the higher the root, the later it is revealed
sections.summary: Speech is rooted in *chachma* and thought in *bina*, yet thought comes first, in a child and even in the essence of the soul, because what is higher in its root is revealed last. So speaking wakes up the thought, and the symbol comes before the thing.

phrases.he: (וזהו מן הדברים הנפלאים וסתומים,
phrases.en: This is an amazing, wondrous, and hidden thing:

phrases.he: למה המחשבה קדמה לדבור,
phrases.en: Why does thought precede speech?

phrases.he: הרי הדבור שרשו בפנימיות ומקור החכמה והמחשבה שרשה בפנימית ומקור דבינה, והחכמה קדמה לבינה שהחכמה נקרא אין ובינה יש כו'
phrases.en: The speech comes from *chachma* and the *machshava* comes from *bina*.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין דבר ואמרת,
שהדבור גבוה בשרשו מאמירה דמחשבה כו'
phrases.en: The *dibur* first comes before the actual *amira* of *machshava*.

phrases.he: וגם מזה עצמו ראיה ממה שאין המחשבה באה בהתחלקות צרופים כי אם בבוא התחלקות הדבור בתנוק כו׳)
phrases.en: It's *davka* when you learn to talk that's when you learn to think, and not the other way around.

blocks.text: **This is an amazing, wondrous, and hidden thing**: why does thought precede speech? Speech is rooted in the inside of *chachma*, thought in *bina*, and *chachma*, called *ayin*, comes before *bina*, called *yesh*. As explained on "*Daber v'amarta*" (speak and say), speech is higher in its root than the saying of thought. And the child proves it: **it's *davka* when you learn to talk that's when you learn to think, and not the other way around**. Otherwise you would learn to think first.

phrases.he: ואף על פי כן ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דבינה דוקא שרש לה׳ גבורות התחלקות דדבור, דאימא אוזיפא כו'
phrases.en: Nonetheless, it's *davka* the division in thought that brings about the division in speech.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב כאמה בתה כו'
phrases.en: Like mother, like daughter: like the thought that's going to be the speech.

phrases.he: ובשרשם הרי הדבור בחכמה, ולכך אבא דוקא יסד ברתא כו'

blocks.text: Even so, **it's *davka* the division in thought that brings about the division in speech**, the mother lending to the daughter: like mother, like daughter, the thought that is going to be the speech. Yet in their root speech is in *chachma*, and so *Abba yasad b'rata*, the father founded the daughter.

phrases.he: וגם מצד שרש הראשון דמחשבה דבור ומעשה כמו שהם קבועים בעצם הנפש הנזכר לעיל, (באות ל"ז) שמבואר שם ג' מדריגות הנזכר לעיל במחשבה שבגלוי כו',
הרי גם שם כלול תחלה אותיות המחשבה בעצם הנפש טרם שכלולה מאותיות הדבור שנקרא רוח ממללא כו'
phrases.en: Even in the *etzem* of the soul with the *hiyuli* letters, the letters of *machshava* precede the letters of speech.

phrases.he: דכמו שבנפש שבאה בגוף קדם המחשבה לדבור ב' שנים, כך בנפש הרוחנית לא נקרא רוח ממללא זמן מה כו'
phrases.en: When the soul is forming, it starts off with letters of thought, and the letters of *dibur* come in later, and only then it can be called the full soul.

phrases.he: והמחשבה כבר יש בה כו'
phrases.en: It already has thought.

blocks.text: The same holds at the first root of thought, speech and action as they are fixed in the essence of the soul, the three levels of chapter 37: **even in the *etzem* of the soul with the *hiyuli* letters, the letters of *machshava* precede the letters of speech**. That is a totally strange thing. You would think that up there it is the other way around, since speech causes thought; yet even there thought comes first, though the soul is called *ruach memalela* (the speaking spirit).

As in the soul in the body thought comes two years before speech, so in the spiritual soul: **when the soul is forming, it starts off with letters of thought, and the letters of *dibur* come in later**, and only then is it the full soul. Thought is already in it.

phrases.he: אם לא שכל דבר הגבוה בשרשו בעצמיות יותר הוא בא באחרונה יותר, שלזה נקרא נפש המדברת דוקא נפש המשכלת,
phrases.en: Whatever is higher in its root comes down farther in actuality. That's why the *nefesh hamaskeles*, the thinking person, is called *davka* the talking person.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת החכמה העצמיות שבה שהוא קודם למחשבה העצמיות שבה כו'
אבל בגלוי בא באחרונה דוקא,
phrases.en: But in revelation, it comes later.

phrases.he: מטעם המבואר במקום אחר באריכות ודי למבין)

blocks.text: Unless, that is, **whatever is higher in its root comes down farther in actuality**. That is why the *nefesh hamaskeles* (the intellectual soul) is called *davka* the speaking soul: the essential *chachma* in it comes before its essential thought, **but in revelation, it comes later**. The real source of speech is higher than thought.

You can see it right now, on the phone: it is *davka* because he wants to talk to the listener that he has to think. Before the call he wasn't thinking about these things, because he wasn't trying to say them. Even had he sat and thought about these very matters, it would not be the same: not trying to say them, he would wake up no new letters.

This is why the Rebbe says that by teaching somebody else you help yourself a thousand times more: having to say it and explain it turns your brain on. So too in *talmud Torah*: say the words, *davka*, and you think them clearer and hold the train of thought far more easily, because speech is connected directly to *chachma*. It is also why it is better to learn *b'chavrusa*, talking it over with the other guy.

blocks.question: Is this also why the *Aibershter* created the world, because it brings it out?
blocks.text: Yes, that is the matter of *dibur*: *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule). The whole matter of speech is that it brings things out, and that is *Malchus* (kingship): bringing it out to somebody else brings out the inner essence.

blocks.title: Matza before the Exodus
blocks.text: This is also the answer to the *minim* (heretics) and their "it's just a symbol", as if the symbol were lower than the actual thing. In reality it is exactly the opposite. They have the whole creation backwards: they think *Pesach* happened, so we made up symbols for it. It was the other way around: the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) wanted certain symbols, so He made *Pesach* for them. You see it because they ate *matza* before they left. We eat *matza* because they left so fast the dough had no time to leaven: a good explanation of why we eat it, but why did they eat it while still there? Because the *Aibershter* wanted *matza* from the start, to show that the symbol precedes the actual thing.
That was the point of an earlier question about names: besides the external name that comes after a thing, there is the internal name that makes the thing in the first place.

blocks.title: The carpenter and the table
blocks.text: Those who say otherwise do not do a proper *hisbonenus*. What do you mean, the name precedes the thing? You have a couch, a chair, a table: those are things, not symbols. Yes, and each one has a name. But the man who made your table had to have the name "table" in his head before he made it; without it he could not have made it. Tell a carpenter to just make something, and you'll give it a symbol once it's made, and he will ask how he is supposed to know what to make: give him the symbol first, and then he knows.

This is what is said, that the Torah preceded the world: the words of Torah came first and the world is made according to them, not the other way around. It is the same thing: *Pesach* was created for the sake of the *matza*. *Matza* is one of the 613 commandments, the limbs of the King, *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King), and they preceded the story of *Pesach*.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*, and what does the rubber stamp show about them?
Why does cutting the car into seats and wheels look like a descent, and why is the power to do it higher than the grasp of the car?
What does the baby who knows which chef's dish he likes show about where the combinations of letters come from?
Why does a speaker only have to think how to take an idea apart, and what happens when he loses the thread?
If speech is rooted in *chachma*, why does thought come first, and what does this say about teaching and saying the words aloud?
